newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down on crown risk.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down on crown risk.

text.p: Czech shares, especially in the banking sector, slid further on Monday with dealers blaming continued uncertainty about interest rate policy and the troubled Czech currency, the crown.
The PX50 index lost 1.1 percent to 503.8 while the major issue dominated RPIX index dropped by 1.8 percent to 1,033.4.
The biggest loser among the major issues was Komercni Banka, the largest domestic commercial bank, which fell 68 crowns, 3.5 percent, to 1,870.
Savings bank Ceska Sporitelna fell six crowns, 2.1 percent, to 285.
"The market is very nervous, foreign investors expect a devaluation/depreciation of the crown...Shares are already very cheap," said Miroslav Nosal of Patria Finance.

The central bank moved to defend the crown on Friday by raising the last resort lending rate, the Lombard, to 50 percenmt from the previous 14 and on Monday hiked the overnight repo rate to 45 percent from 12.9.
In response, Komercni Banka raised its reference rate on Monday afternoon to 24.6 percent from 12.3 percent.
